chunks: A man said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: “Indeed, I am sometimes in travel and cannot find the qiblah at night.”
So he said: “Do you know the star that is called al-Jady?” I said: “Yes.”
He said: “Then place it on your right, and when you are on the road of hajj, then place it between your shoulders.”

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state of being on a journey
key_terms.الْجَدْيَ: al-Jady, the star identified for orientation
key_terms.الْكَوْكَبَ: the star used as a point of direction
key_terms.طَرِيقِ الْحَجِّ: the route of hajj; the pilgrimage road
key_terms.كَتِفَيْكَ: your two shoulders; the bodily reference for alignment
key_terms.يَمِينِكَ: your right side; the directional placement mentioned by the Imam

ai.seo_question: How can a traveler determine the qiblah at night according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical ruling for determining the qiblah during travel at night by using the star called al-Jady. It reflects the Imam’s guidance in acts of worship, especially salat (prayer), when ordinary means of orientation are difficult.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.860 - A man said to Imam Al-Sadiq (as):
"I am sometimes traveling and cannot determine the Qiblah at night."
The Imam asked: "Do you know the star that is called 'al-Jady' (the North Star)?"
The man replied: "Yes."
The Imam said: "Place it to your right, and if you are on the pilgrimage route, place it between your shoulders”.
